key_insight: LLM evaluators can spot real radiology report errors, but they often over-penalize harmless wording changes, so clinical significance is harder to judge than a simple score suggests.
clinical_relevance: For radiology report generation, better metrics can reduce misleading evaluations and help prioritize mistakes that could affect patient care.
method: Tested 8 LLM-based evaluators on the ReEvalMed benchmark.
Measured two aspects: discrimination of true clinical errors and robustness to harmless variation.
Trained lightweight metrics on 4k synthetic report pairs using Qwen3-8B and MedGemma-4B.
evidence_signal: Across one-pass and two-pass settings, the study found a widespread discrimination bias, and the trained metric outperformed 32B-scale medical LLMs while staying competitive with proprietary models.
watch_item: Even strong metrics may still trade off error detection against robustness, and two-pass inference adds cost without consistent overall gains.
paper_title: Beyond Scalar Scores: Exploring LLM-based Metrics for Clinical Significance Evaluation in Radiology Reports
